title: Protocol for tracking the inheritance patterns of proteins in live Saccharomyces cerevisiae cells using a photo-convertible fluorescent protein
protocol: Streak cells from a glycerol stock onto a YPD agar plate.
Incubate the streaked plate at 30°C for 3 days.
Inoculate 5 ml of synthetic medium with a single yeast colony expressing Protein of Interest fused to Dendra2.
Incubate overnight (∼16 hours) in an incubator shaker at 30°C and 220 rpm.
Measure the OD600 of the culture from Day 1.
Calculate the volume needed for inoculating 20 ml synthetic medium to achieve an initial OD600 of ∼0.3.
Inoculate 20 mL of synthetic medium with the calculated volume of overnight culture.
Incubate overnight (∼16 hours) at 30°C and 220 rpm.
Check that the OD600 is around 0.3.
Let yeast grow at 30°C, 220 rpm until OD600 ∼0.5–0.8.
Add nocodazole (15 μg/mL final) for 3 h if G2/M arrest is needed.
Preheat table top centrifuge to 30°C.
Spin cells for 2 min at 3000×g in a table top centrifuge with a swinging bucket rotor.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cells in 20 mL of fresh synthetic medium.
Let yeast grow for 45 min at 30°C, 220 rpm.
Prepare 10 mL of 0.8% agarose in synthetic medium with the desired carbon source.
Fill all 8 wells with liquid agarose solution (~350 μL per well) and let the gel solidify.
Use a sterile 10 μL pipette tip to carefully lift the gels and place them vertically on the side of each well.
Wait a few minutes for the bottom of the well to dry.
Put 3 μL of yeast cell suspension into each well and spread the liquid with the pipette tip.
Let dry for 10 s to 2 min.
Carefully put the agarose gel back on top of the cells without trapping bubbles.
Cover the slide with its lid.
Warm up the suspension in a microwave oven until agarose is dissolved.
Fill all 8 wells with agarose solution (∼350 μL per well).
Let the agarose solidify.
Measure the OD600 of the yeast culture.
Spin the entire culture for 2 min at 3000×g in a swinging bucket rotor preheated at 30°C.
Remove supernatant and re-suspend cell pellet in synthetic medium to a final OD600 ∼2.2.
Pipette 3 μL of re-suspended yeast cells into each well.
Spread the cells with the pipette tip.
Let dry until there are no more visible liquid droplets on the bottom of the well (10 s to 2 min).
Carefully place the agarose gel back down, on top of the cells and avoid trapping bubbles.
Adjust the laser power for the 488 nm laser to ∼360 μW.
Set the laser power for the 561 nm laser to ∼300 μW.
Adjust the LED photo-conversion lamp (390 nm) to ∼2.30 mW.
Set the temperature of the thermostatic chamber surrounding the microscope stage to 30°C.
Choose 5 positions per well for imaging, totaling 40 positions.
Set Z stack parameters with 5 stacks separated by 1 μm between each pair.
Take one image at each position in the Led Trans mode and at 488 nm excitation wavelength.
Take one image at each position in the Led Trans mode and at 561 nm excitation wavelength.
Expose cells to 390 nm UV light from the LED Lamp for 1 min at 60% capacity with Neutral Density filters ND4 or ND8.
Set up automated time-lapse image acquisition.
Take one photo in LED Trans mode for each position.
Capture a photo at 488 nm excitation wavelength with GFP emission filter for each position.
Capture a photo at 561 nm excitation wavelength with TAMRA emission filter for each position.
Adjust camera gain and exposure times empirically to avoid signal saturation.
Take photos every 6.5 minutes for 6.5 hours or adjust time intervals based on microscope speed to obtain 61 photos per position.
Process images using ImageJ and a custom macro provided in the supplementary file.
Merge the 5 Z stack projections into one image.
Keep maximum intensity pixels from each stack during merging.
Merge LED Trans, 488 nm, and 561 nm channels and display them by color.
Concatenate all 61 time points into one file.
Start BudJ after opening the image.
Choose the parameters for BudJ analysis.
Adjust the parameters according to cell size and image quality.
Use a scale factor of 1 micron/pixel instead of the actual scale factor to speed up analysis.
Note that the max cell radius parameter of 20 microns corresponds to 5.34 microns in real scale.
Scale cell dimensions measured by BudJ according to the real scale factor if using an artificial scale factor of 1.
Choose one cell as the Mother cell for tracking in all 61 frames.
Identify the time points when the fluorescent signal has been fully transferred from the mother to daughter 1 and daughter 2 (magenta arrow).
Click on the mother at time 1, the first daughter at time 11, and the second daughter at time 22.
BudJ will track all three cells until the last frame and record red and green fluorescence intensities in each cell in every frame.
